title: Simple linear regression
statement: Fit y ≈ b·x + a by ordinary least squares. Return [b, a] (relative error ≤ 10⁻⁶). The x values are not all equal. Watch numerical stability: one test has x near 10⁸.
hints: b = Cov(x, y) / Var(x); a = ȳ − b·x̄.
Centre the data first: Σx² − n·x̄² cancels catastrophically when x is large.

solution.explanation: The normal equations for one regressor reduce to b = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) / Σ(x − x̄)², a = ȳ − b x̄. The "textbook" form with Σx² − n x̄² loses all precision when x ≈ 10⁸ (catastrophic cancellation in floating point), so always centre first. That is the stability lesson behind every regression library (QR rather than normal equations for many regressors).
solution.python:
def ols_fit(x, y):
    n = len(x); mx = sum(x) / n; my = sum(y) / n
    sxy = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(x, y)); sxx = sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in x)
    b = sxy / sxx
    return [b, my - b * mx]
